title: horizontalOrdinaryUpperComparison
statement: Let f:X→Y, g:S→Y and h:T→S be morphisms of schemes. Put A=X×_Y S, P=A×_S T and Q=X×_Y T. Let e:P≅Q be the canonical iterated pullback isomorphism, and let v1:A→X, v2:P→A and u:Q→X be the first projections [def-pc-fibre-product]. On the derived QCoh categories [def-pc-derived-category], define the upper comparison from the successive first-projection pullbacks to outer first-projection pullback followed by pullback along e=the canonical iterated pullback isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. It is horizontalMateComp(v2,v1), the equality transport along e.hom≫u=v2≫v1, and horizontalMateComp(e.hom,u).symm, in this order [lem-sc-horizontal-duality-mate-comparisons]. This is the pinned upper comparison with the QCoh functors displayed explicitly.

source.place: Remark 20.28.5 (0ATM), Remark 20.28.3 (08HY), Lemma 20.27.2 (0D5S); fixed comparisons used in Lemma 48.5.2 (0ATR)

proof.text: Compose horizontalMateComp(v2,v1), the equality isomorphism induced by the first-projection equation for the canonical iterated pullback isomorphism, and horizontalMateComp(e.hom,u).symm. The QCoh restriction functor names in the signature are definitionally equal to the horizontal names. This definition uses no direct-image comparison or inverse equivalence unit.

def horizontalOrdinaryUpperComparison
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    {X Y S T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : S ⟶ Y) (h : T ⟶ S) :
    qcPullback (pullback.fst f g) ⋙ qcPullback (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f g) h) ≅
      qcPullback (pullback.fst f (h ≫ g)) ⋙
        qcPullback (pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso f g h).hom
